title: Roos computation of derived limits of abelian groups
statement: Let $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ be the category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] of abelian groups and $\varprojlim:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the inverse-limit functor. Then $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives and $\varprojlim$ is left exact additive, so its right derived functors $R^q\varprojlim$ are defined [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For an inverse system $(A_n,f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ of abelian groups let $1-s:\prod_nA_n\to\prod_nA_n$ be the map $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1}))_n$. Then, naturally in $(A_n)$, $\varprojlim_nA_n=\ker(1-s)$, $R^1\varprojlim_nA_n\cong\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$, and $R^q\varprojlim_nA_n=0$ for every $q\geq2$.

proof.text: The tower category is abelian by Mathlib functorCategoryAbelian. The existing proof roosTowerEnoughInjectives constructs an injective presentation using tower_injective_embedding and injective_of_injective_split_tower. The right derived functors are therefore defined.

proof.text: Construct the canonical map from limit A to product A_n. Its composite with 1-s is zero by limit compatibility. The projections of kernel(1-s) satisfy the adjacent compatibility equations by the kernel condition, and NatTrans.ofOpSequence extends them to a cone over A. Its universal map into limit A is inverse to the canonical kernel lift, as checked after each projection. Naturality follows by cancellation of the kernel inclusion and product extensionality. Commutation of product maps with 1-s is towerTransitionEndomorphism_natural_backward applied to naturality of the tower morphism.

proof.text: Use the functorial length-one limit-acyclic resolution of [lem-pc-roos-functorial-acyclic-resolution]. Its data give a short exact sequence S(A) with first term A, and natural isomorphisms of the limits of the other terms with the levelwise product, identifying the induced differential with 1-s.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: finite-prefix systems B and C

proof.text: Apply exists_horseshoe_rightDerived_deltaFunctor to lim, and identify its family of functors with lim.rightDerived. Compose the degree-zero comparison rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf with the two product identifications. Transport the exact segment R^0 lim U(A) -> R^0 lim V(A) -> R^1 lim A to product A -> product A -> R^1 lim A. Vanishing of R^1 lim U(A) makes the connecting map epi, so exactness gives its cokernel universal property and the unique isomorphism R^1 lim A -> cokernel(1-s). For a tower map, naturality of the resolution and of the connecting map gives naturality of this isomorphism after cancellation of the epi connecting map. For q=n+1>=2, exactness of R^n lim V(A) -> R^(n+1) lim A -> R^(n+1) lim U(A), whose outer objects vanish by the resolution, implies the middle object is zero.
